bridges.description: Show that the observed degree and distribution of fundamental religious disagreement are more expected if God does not exist than if God exists.
Establish that a truth-valuing relational God would have reason to correct consequential false beliefs that impair willing, informed relationship.
Distinguish generic supernatural belief from independently convergent detailed doctrine and explain why the latter counterfactual sharpens the evidential comparison.
Show that agreement or disagreement alone underdetermines theism versus atheism, so the observed disagreement need not support atheism.
Identify coherent divine reasons for permitting disagreement, including formation, staged teaching, freedom and accommodation, that weaken the proposed expectation.
Show that relationship and fair judgment need not require uniform detailed doctrine because acquaintance, general moral awareness and response to available evidence can matter.
